---

## Owner ruling 2026-09-13 — a code value confirmed by research is upgraded; the empty circle is for code WITHOUT research backing

> **"Sometimes code standards come from T1. If a code standard is being confirmed as genuine best
> practice according to studies, then the code/regulatory input can be upgraded."**
>
> **"It is when a code/regulatory input does not have research backing that it gets the empty circle."**

**What this settles.** It was put to the owner as one of three band questions raised by the
2026-09-13 design pass: what strength a cell carries when its *finding* is T1 but its only *value*
comes from a code. The answer is the upgrade route, and it is ruled — not the two-part rendering
that was also on the table.

**WHAT IT EXTENDS, AND THE EXTENSION IS THE POINT.** `evidence-architecture.md`'s **G1** re-grains a
T4/T5 source out of NON-ANCHORING on exactly one trigger: *"its evidence basis is documented as
traceable to T1/T2 evidence, with that provenance recorded on the source record."* That is a
**genealogy** test — where the number came from. This ruling adds a second, independent route:
**confirmation** — a study finding the code's value sound, whether or not anyone can trace how the
committee reached it. The two are not the same test and the corpus already separates them:
**REF-00980** concludes *"changes to the technical requirements for ramp slope and length cannot be
recommended at this time."* It establishes nothing about ADA's provenance. Under G1 as written it
re-grains nothing. Under this ruling it upgrades the value it confirms.

**And it makes the empty circle CONDITIONAL where it was automatic.** `tier-system.md` §5 maps T6
(code-floor) to `○` flatly, and §8's band table gives `○ Weak` to "T6 (code-floor)" with a cell whose
entire basis is T4–T6 taking `○` regardless. After this ruling `○` marks the **unbacked** case
specifically: a code or regulatory input with no research behind it. A code value a study has
confirmed is no longer `○` by virtue of being a code.

**WHAT THE RULING DOES NOT SAY, recorded so nobody fills it in silently.** Three things.
(1) **Which band an upgraded value lands in** — the ruling says "upgraded", not "upgraded to ●". The
natural reading is that it takes the band of the confirming evidence, so a T1 confirmation yields
`●`; that is a reading, not the ruling, and it is the next thing to put to the owner.
(2) **Whether T4/T5 and T6 behave alike here.** The ruling says "code/regulatory input" without
distinguishing them, while existing doctrine splits them — `◐` for T4/T5 citations, `○` for T6.
(3) **What counts as confirmation.** REF-00980's non-recommendation of change is the clear case. A
study that merely *uses* a code value as its rig setting is not confirming it, and that distinction
is exactly what the `confirms` / `tested_at` edges of migration 075 exist to record.

**Mechanism, so this is executable rather than aspirational.** The 075 design gives the row-level
vocabulary: a `confirms` edge from a finding row to the code figure it confirms is the upgrade
trigger; `tested_at` is not; `insufficient` is the opposite and remains an open band question. The
engine rule that reads those edges is not yet built, so **the upgrade is ruled and unexecuted** —
which is the state an empty table should be read as, per the 2026-09-11 entry above.

CONDITION: Any session assigning a strength band to a determination whose value comes from a code or
regulatory source, or citing G1's traceability clause as the only re-graining route.
ACTION: Treat confirmation-by-study as a second re-graining route alongside documented traceability.
Read `○` as "no research backing", not as "is a code". Record the confirming relation on the row
rather than asserting the upgrade in prose. Do not assume which band an upgraded value takes — that
is unruled.
DATE: 2026-09-13 — owner ruling, quoted above.
EOF

content.text:
Two things worth knowing before I record it.

**The good news:** you already ratified a *weighted-strength anchor model* — `tier-system.md` §8, DR-2026-07-20 — so today's ruling extends an existing frame rather than opening a new one.

**The problem:** §8 assigns bands by **membership**, not by any number. T1/Co-1/T2/Co-2/T3-clinical → ●; T4/T5 → ◐; T3-grey/T6 → ○. There are **no numeric tier weights anywhere in the project**. And the one column that looks like it holds them — `weighting_profile.tier_weights` — doesn't: all five rows hold audience *foregrounding* lists like `{"foreground":["T1","CO1",...]}`, which tiers to show first for a designer versus a policymaker. A future implementer hunting for the weights will find that column and be misled.

**And your example constrains the function more than it first appears.** Score the bands ●=3, ◐=2, ○=1. Two T1 plus one T4 is (3+3+2)/3 = **2.67**, which rounds *up* to ● — not the half circle you named. So the obvious implementation fails your own worked example. Rounding **down** gives ◐, which matches. I'm recording that as a reading to confirm, not as your ruling.

Reproduces your example exactly, and the arithmetic is now pinned. One property falls out of `floor` that's worth naming:

```
2×T1 + 1×T4   → ◐   (mean 2.667)   ← your example
3×T1          → ●   (mean 3.000)
2×T1 + 1×T6   → ◐   (mean 2.333)
1×T1 + 2×T6   → ○   (mean 1.667)
99×T1 + 1×T4  → ◐   (mean 2.990)
```

**Why `075_extraction_relations.sql` stays untracked.** CLAUDE.md rule 3: migrations are *append-only and immutable once committed — fix forward with a compensating migration.* A normal file committed half-written gets fixed by editing it. So committing that file right now would enshrine whatever state the agent happens to have left it in, before it has run `--rebuild`, before its table-level CHECKs have been fault-injected, and before I've confirmed `dbcore.WRITABLE_TABLES` gained the junction — which, if missed, means the capture path silently drops every edge the migration exists to create.

The hook is asking for something that is right for ordinary files and wrong for this one. It'll keep asking until the agent reports; that's the correct cost.

input.title: research: batch 07 lands provisional, four scope rulings executed, and five owner rulings on banding
input.body:
**This body was rewritten 2026-09-13 02:0x.** It previously described a two-file status note and said "No code, no schema, no database" — false since the branch grew to 25 commits. The original framing is preserved at the foot.

## What this branch now does

**Batch 07 ran and landed.** `specification_id 2` — parameter 2 (`TERM-002 corridor width`) × `MOB` on `accessible-circulation-geometry` — state **`provisional`**, `tier_basis T3-only`. The parameter was *promoted* from base vocabulary, not coined: running the runbook's `observe-term → add-term` path as written would have minted "corridor clear width" beside TERM-002, the near-duplicate defect `ORDER-OF-WORK.md` caught with `turning diameter` beside TERM-003. Gate COMPLIANT on all 19 rules.

**The finding, which is content and not just corpus state:** not one retrieved source states an absolute corridor width. Koontz reports only that code-compliant space fails 10–100% of users; the scooter study that no scooter completed its manoeuvres within the space existing standards allow; the Japanese survey a required *enlargement* of >30 cm. The literature reachable from here measures the **inadequacy of dimensions** rather than the dimensions.

**The Co-1 leg is a genuine zero** — 0 with the co-production clause, 30 without it. A venue fact, not a query-shape failure, which is the distinction R14 exists to force.

**B5b's four scope rulings were executed from bytes.** REF-00784 moved tier 1 → 3 on its own abstract's word ("Case series", "sample of convenience"), fifty-four days after the anchor sweep recorded that tier 1 was wrong. All 11 sources are now tier-consistent; `adjudication_integrity` PASSES.

## Defects found by tripping them

- **H05** — `log-search` guarded "the count and the edges are the same fact" with a condition on `ids` being non-empty, so an admission count with **no** `--admitted-ref-id` was never checked. 8 of 13 executions in canonical carry that shape, one of them batch 06's, which the DoD gate had passed COMPLIANT. Closed.
- **`check_values` was losing real vocabulary values**, not only leaking comment text: bare parens inside SQL comments truncated the extractor's scan. `gap_mining.outcome` was reporting 2 of its 5 legitimate values. Closed, with a new blocking check M01, mutation-tested.
- **`add-source`'s duplicate-DOI pre-check** was exact-match and ignored the locator stash. Closed.
- **The retrieval manifest recorded curl's exit code, not HTTP status**, so a fetched 404 logged as a successful retrieval — in the one record that establishes a source was really retrieved. Closed.
- **`tier` was reachable by no sanctioned writer**, which is why REF-00784's tier sat wrong for fifty-four days. `amend-source --tier` added, admissible only beside `--field scope` and only equal to what the ladder derives.

## Adversarial passes changed the filed rows

An antagonist armed itself independently *before* the batch ran; a Fable read-only pass then interrogated the whole pipeline. Two findings changed data rather than being noted: REF-00982's extraction was **retracted** (its own abstract says the objective is to demonstrate a re-sampling method — the widths are the illustration, and `door width` is TERM-021, a separate term), and REF-00971's was marked **`contested`** on the turning-space challenge. The antagonist also predicted `provisional / T3-only` before the engine ran.

## Five owner rulings, recorded in `references/project-standards.md`

1. A code value **confirmed by research is upgraded**; `○` marks *unbacked* code. Extends G1's traceability test with a second route — confirmation, not just genealogy.
2. **Derived figures take a weighted average** of their inputs, not the weakest. Overturns the design pass's recommendation.
3. An **`insufficient` finding supplies direction, not value** — queried before recording, because the other reading of the phrase would have discarded the project's R7 harm evidence.
4. **Grey literature echoing a code value** is regulatory stratum, not an independent root.
5. The weighting function: **floored mean of band ordinals**. The owner's 2×T1 + 1×T4 = ◐ case is the acceptance test and falsifies rounding to nearest.

## Also

- **Batch 06 was closed, nine days late** — it left no session record, no attestation, and both pointers naming batch 05, so its two Tier 1 admissions went un-audited by every session-scoped check. `test_db_integrity`'s L04 forced the issue. The record is labelled a reconstruction and its attestation covers the reconstruction act, not batch 06's conduct: a first-person statement about another session would be fabricated continuity.
- Both migrations were rehearsed against a copy of canonical before apply; `foreign_key_check` empty both sides.
- `run_checks --changed-from origin/main` PASS, no blocking failures, **blocking-and-vacuous now 0**.

**Known and deliberately not swept:** `validate_reasoning` fails advisory on `references/bpc-reasoning/room-acoustic-performance.md`, pre-existing debt this branch never touched — it became visible only because these `sessions/` paths pulled a dormant check into scope.

---

<details><summary>Original body, 2026-09-12 — accurate for the first two commits only</summary>

Answered "can we perform research, and where are we at" by deriving the state rather than quoting the plan documents. Verdict: research was not blocked and had already run; of B1–B7, six and a half were closed, and what remained was B5b — four `evidence_sources` rows with `scope` NULL, making their stored tiers underivable and the rows non-anchoring. Those four were the sources that measured corridor geometry, which was the planned batch 07 cell.

</details>

standards; and a width the extractor computed from stock plus 30 cm,

not four column sets: columns cannot hold N inputs of a derivation or N conditions
of a tuple, and a baseline pointer at a SOURCE loses which FIGURE of that source is
the baseline -- ADA 405 states slope, run and landing, and the baseline of a slope
finding is the slope figure while the run figure is a condition on it. So the
referent is an extraction row, which forces a standard's tuple to exist as rows:
one shape serves the baseline problem and the conditioned-tuple problem together.

table-level CHECKs, two indexes, one view. No DROP, no table rebuild, so D-0168's

canonical and on a full rebuild.

v_derived_figure_check recomputes a derived figure from its base and delta inputs

Migration 075 is in — `f5f4797`, canonical at `user_version 75`.

**What landed.** Two nullable columns on the extraction row (`figure_role`, `comparator`) and a junction table carrying typed edges between figures: `tested_at`, `audited_against`, `confirms`, `insufficient`, `delta_over`, `condition_on`, `derived_from`. **What I verified rather than accepted from the agent:**

- The rebuild replays 19 schema + 53 data migrations to version 75, `foreign_key_check` empty.
- All six table-level CHECKs and both column CHECKs fault-injected — **nine refusals, each rejecting the row it exists to reject**, with four happy-path shapes accepted. A CHECK I haven't seen refuse is a CHECK I haven't tested.
- **No UNIQUE index on `source_value_extractions`**, on canonical and on the rebuild — D-0168's ruled absence survives, which is the thing an additive migration could most easily have broken.
- `dbcore.WRITABLE_TABLES` gained `extraction_relations` at line 615. Without it `emit_batch_sql` drops every edge silently and the whole migration writes nothing.
- Both Pydantic mirrors report zero drift.

**On sequencing:** I applied 075 to canonical in the same change rather than committing the file first. `migration_reproducibility` is blocking and fails for as long as a migration sits on disk at a version canonical hasn't reached — it went green on apply, and the battery came back `PASS`, no blocking failures, blocking-and-vacuous 0.

**What deliberately did not land: any writer.** No `db.py` verb sets `figure_role` or writes an edge. `NULL` means "not yet graded", and §8 argues against argparse plumbing with nothing behind it. So the table exists and is empty — which, per the 2026-09-11 entry in the ledger, should be read as *ruled and unexecuted*, not as an open question. The five rulings you gave tonight are exactly the rules the engine will read those edges under.

A research batch ran end to end. A second determination exists. Five genuine code defects are closed — an admission count that claimed edges it didn't have, a parser silently dropping real vocabulary values, an exact-match DOI check, a 404 logging as a successful retrieval, and a tier no sanctioned writer could touch. Two new blocking checks, both mutation-tested.

**Here's the part you're right about.**

`extraction_relations`: **0 rows.** `figure_role` on all 8 extractions: **NULL**. `value_min`/`value_max` on both determinations: **NULL**. So after all of tonight, **the guidebook contains no corridor width and no ramp gradient.** Not one number reached the book.

And there's a worse version of that. Tonight I *added* apparatus — a migration, a junction table, two blocking checks — while content output stayed where it was. The project's own operative instrument names that failure: DR-2026-08-19 §11 warns about sessions that commit "something other than search logs, migrations or a rendered determination." Batch 07 clears that bar by a hair, and only a hair.

**The chain that stops a width reaching the book, in order:**

2. **No writer exists.** No `db.py` verb sets `figure_role` or writes an edge. The agent declined to build one, correctly under §8 — but it means the 8 live extractions **cannot be graded**. ❌
3. The engine reads none of the new fields, so your five rulings are recorded and inert. ❌
4. Nothing resolves a value, so `specifications.value_min` stays NULL regardless. ❌

Step 2 is the bottleneck and it's fully specified — `add-extraction` flags, `relate-extraction`, `amend-extraction`, `derive-extraction`, each with its refusals written out. It's mechanical work, and until it exists tonight's migration is a table nobody can put a row in.

Want me to build the writers now? That's the step that converts everything above from machinery into something you can actually run against the eight rows we already have.

input.prompt:
Repository: /home/user/guidebook. You own ONE file: `scripts/db.py`. Do NOT touch `tools/`, `scripts/audit/`, `governance/` or `scripts/dbcore.py` — another agent owns those. Make the edits, PROVE every refusal by fault injection, then STOP: do NOT git commit, do NOT git push. The orchestrator verifies and commits.

Read CLAUDE.md first. The rules binding you hardest: rule 3 (never write `data/guidebook.db` — use a scratch copy under `GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH` passed INLINE on every call, the harness resets env between shells), rule 4 (sweep the callers), section 4 (`db.py` refuses, and that is its whole value — vocabularies come from the column's own CHECK via `dbcore.check_values`, never a list in code), and section 5(c) (a fabricated citation passing green gates is a real failure this project has suffered).

## Context

Migration 075 landed today (`scripts/migrations/075_extraction_relations.sql` — read it first, its comments carry the vocabulary meanings). It added to `source_value_extractions` two nullable columns — `figure_role` (`claim|finding|condition|derived`) and `comparator` (`=|<|<=|>|>=|between|approx`) — and a junction `extraction_relations` with relations `tested_at|audited_against|confirms|insufficient|exceeds|delta_over|condition_on|derived_from`, a referent that is either `to_extraction_id` (a row) or `to_label`+`to_kind` (`standard|own_sample|prior_source|unnamed`), a `stated` field (`named|unnamed|inferred`), an `input_role` (`base|delta|factor`, iff `derived_from`), and a mandatory `quote`.

**The table has zero rows and no writer. Your job is the writer.** Until it exists nobody can grade the 8 live extractions and the migration is a table nobody can put a row in.

## What to build

**1. `add-extraction` gains flags** (parser around `scripts/db.py:1163`, function `insert_extraction` around `:3564`):
`--figure-role` (REQUIRED), `--comparator`, and a repeatable relation group: `--relation` (REQUIRED; accepts the literal `none`), `--to-extraction N` | `--to-label "..."` with `--to-kind`, `--stated`, `--quote "..."`, `--input-role`. Add `figure_role` and `comparator` to the column list the INSERT builds and to `_SVE_VOCAB_COLUMNS` so `dbcore.check_declared` validates them from the schema.

**2. `relate-extraction`** — add an edge to an existing row: `--from N --relation R [--to-extraction M | --to-label L --to-kind K] --stated S --quote Q [--input-role I] --session`. Plus a `--repoint` mode: given an existing label edge and `--to-extraction M`, NULL the label and kind, set the target, and ledger the old label into `notes`. That is how an "ADAAG" label edge becomes a real row pointer once ADA §405 is admitted and extracted.

**3. `amend-extraction`** — `--extraction-id N --field {figure_role,comparator} --value V --reason "..." --session`. Refuse every other field: a wrong `claimed_value` or `claim_text` is a SECOND ROW and a contest, not an overwrite (D-0168; `add-population-match` deliberately permits a dissenting second row for the same reason). Append `|| <date> <field> SET <old> -> <new> (<reason>)` to `notes`, the append discipline `amend-search` already uses.

**4. `derive-extraction`** — writes a `figure_role='derived'` row plus two `derived_from` edges: `--ref-id --slug --parameter-id` + lens flags `--base N --delta M [--claimed-value V --claimed-unit U --comparator C] --claim-text "..." --session`. Set `root_type='derived_calculation'` and `root_ref_id` from the base row.

## The refusals — each must be fault-injected before you report

Wording matters; these are teaching messages in the house style (say what is wrong, why, and what to do instead). Read existing refusals in `insert_extraction` for the register.

- `--figure-role` missing → required. Reason to convey: a value with no role reads as a claim, and a tested slope read as a claim is how `1:20, 1:16, 1:12, 1:8` became a `range` no source ever asserted (that is live extraction 1 in the corpus).
- `--relation` missing → required; `none` is the way to say the source states its figure absolutely. Reason: five of five corridor-width sources state theirs against a reference they name or invoke, so silence is not "absolute", it is "unchecked".
- `figure_role='claim'` combined with `--relation insufficient` or `audited_against` → refuse: a row finding the baseline inadequate asserts no absolute value; grade it `finding`. If the source also states a value that is a second row.
- `figure_role='derived'` without at least one `derived_from` edge carrying `--input-role base` → refuse.
- `claim_type='absent'` with `figure_role` other than `finding` → refuse: absence is a finding.
- `--relation delta_over` without `--comparator` on the row → refuse: "more than thirty centimetres" is `>` 30, and storing 30 turns a floor into a point.
- `--to-label` with `--stated named` where `--quote` does not contain the label as a byte-substring → refuse.
- **THE IMPORTANT ONE — `--quote` must occur byte-for-byte in a persisted retrieval artefact for this `--ref-id`.** Implement by importing `retrieval_log` and using `_manifest_records(session)` across every `retrieval-log/*/` directory, then `read_bytes()` on each named artefact. **Do NOT use `_logged_payloads`** — it keeps JSON only and would drop the XML that carries abstracts. Refusal names both possibilities: either the payload was never persisted (R10 — retrieve first) or the quote came from memory (section 5(c)). A sibling change added a `status` field to manifest lines; your reader must tolerate its presence and its absence.
- `--to-extraction` must exist, must differ from `--from`, and for `condition_on`/`derived_from` must share `--ref-id` with the asserting row unless `--cross-source` is passed with a reason (a condition drawn from another document is a synthesis act; make it explicit).
- `derive-extraction`: base and delta must share `claimed_unit` unless `--claimed-unit` is given with a `--conversion-note`; and when both parse as numbers, `--claimed-value` must equal base + delta — refuse with both numbers named. A derived figure that disagrees with its own inputs is the defect this verb exists to prevent.

Write the row and its edges in ONE transaction — the `add-term` precedent, where the term and its adjudication land together. Return JSON naming the extraction_id, the figure_role and the edges written.

## Prove it

Work on `cp data/guidebook.db $SCRATCH/w.db` with `GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH` inline. Fault-inject EVERY refusal above and show its message. Then show four happy paths actually writing: a `claim` with `--relation none`; a `finding` with an `insufficient` edge to a `--to-label` (use REF-00784's real quote about Accessibility Guidelines, which is in `retrieval-log/session_2026-09-12-b5b-scope-rulings/f5d94e0feaa8d48f.xml`); a `condition` with a `condition_on` edge to another row; and a `derive-extraction` that correctly refuses because no base row exists. Confirm `sha256sum data/guidebook.db` is unchanged at the end.

Also run `python3 scripts/tests/test_db_integrity.py` and `python3 scripts/run_checks.py --selftest` — both must stay green.

## Report

Every flag and refusal with file:line, the fault-injection output for each, the happy paths, anything you chose not to build and why. If part of this brief is wrong or unsafe, say so and leave it undone — a reasoned refusal beats a forced edit. Do not commit.

Repository: /home/user/guidebook. You own ONE file: `scripts/db.py`. Do NOT touch `tools/`, `scripts/audit/`, `governance/` or `scripts/dbcore.py` — another agent owns those. Make the edits, PROVE every refusal by fault injection, then STOP: do NOT git commit, do NOT git push. The orchestrator verifies and commits.

Read CLAUDE.md first. The rules binding you hardest: rule 3 (never write `data/guidebook.db` — use a scratch copy under `GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH` passed INLINE on every call, the harness resets env between shells), rule 4 (sweep the callers), section 4 (`db.py` refuses, and that is its whole value — vocabularies come from the column's own CHECK via `dbcore.check_values`, never a list in code), and section 5(c) (a fabricated citation passing green gates is a real failure this project has suffered).

## Context

Migration 075 landed today (`scripts/migrations/075_extraction_relations.sql` — read it first, its comments carry the vocabulary meanings). It added to `source_value_extractions` two nullable columns — `figure_role` (`claim|finding|condition|derived`) and `comparator` (`=|<|<=|>|>=|between|approx`) — and a junction `extraction_relations` with relations `tested_at|audited_against|confirms|insufficient|exceeds|delta_over|condition_on|derived_from`, a referent that is either `to_extraction_id` (a row) or `to_label`+`to_kind` (`standard|own_sample|prior_source|unnamed`), a `stated` field (`named|unnamed|inferred`), an `input_role` (`base|delta|factor`, iff `derived_from`), and a mandatory `quote`.

**The table has zero rows and no writer. Your job is the writer.** Until it exists nobody can grade the 8 live extractions and the migration is a table nobody can put a row in.

## What to build

**1. `add-extraction` gains flags** (parser around `scripts/db.py:1163`, function `insert_extraction` around `:3564`):
`--figure-role` (REQUIRED), `--comparator`, and a repeatable relation group: `--relation` (REQUIRED; accepts the literal `none`), `--to-extraction N` | `--to-label "..."` with `--to-kind`, `--stated`, `--quote "..."`, `--input-role`. Add `figure_role` and `comparator` to the column list the INSERT builds and to `_SVE_VOCAB_COLUMNS` so `dbcore.check_declared` validates them from the schema.

**2. `relate-extraction`** — add an edge to an existing row: `--from N --relation R [--to-extraction M | --to-label L --to-kind K] --stated S --quote Q [--input-role I] --session`. Plus a `--repoint` mode: given an existing label edge and `--to-extraction M`, NULL the label and kind, set the target, and ledger the old label into `notes`. That is how an "ADAAG" label edge becomes a real row pointer once ADA §405 is admitted and extracted.

**3. `amend-extraction`** — `--extraction-id N --field {figure_role,comparator} --value V --reason "..." --session`. Refuse every other field: a wrong `claimed_value` or `claim_text` is a SECOND ROW and a contest, not an overwrite (D-0168; `add-population-match` deliberately permits a dissenting second row for the same reason). Append `|| <date> <field> SET <old> -> <new> (<reason>)` to `notes`, the append discipline `amend-search` already uses.

**4. `derive-extraction`** — writes a `figure_role='derived'` row plus two `derived_from` edges: `--ref-id --slug --parameter-id` + lens flags `--base N --delta M [--claimed-value V --claimed-unit U --comparator C] --claim-text "..." --session`. Set `root_type='derived_calculation'` and `root_ref_id` from the base row.

## The refusals — each must be fault-injected before you report

Wording matters; these are teaching messages in the house style (say what is wrong, why, and what to do instead). Read existing refusals in `insert_extraction` for the register.

- `--figure-role` missing → required. Reason to convey: a value with no role reads as a claim, and a tested slope read as a claim is how `1:20, 1:16, 1:12, 1:8` became a `range` no source ever asserted (that is live extraction 1 in the corpus).
- `--relation` missing → required; `none` is the way to say the source states its figure absolutely. Reason: five of five corridor-width sources state theirs against a reference they name or invoke, so silence is not "absolute", it is "unchecked".
- `figure_role='claim'` combined with `--relation insufficient` or `audited_against` → refuse: a row finding the baseline inadequate asserts no absolute value; grade it `finding`. If the source also states a value that is a second row.
- `figure_role='derived'` without at least one `derived_from` edge carrying `--input-role base` → refuse.
- `claim_type='absent'` with `figure_role` other than `finding` → refuse: absence is a finding.
- `--relation delta_over` without `--comparator` on the row → refuse: "more than thirty centimetres" is `>` 30, and storing 30 turns a floor into a point.
- `--to-label` with `--stated named` where `--quote` does not contain the label as a byte-substring → refuse.
- **THE IMPORTANT ONE — `--quote` must occur byte-for-byte in a persisted retrieval artefact for this `--ref-id`.** Implement by importing `retrieval_log` and using `_manifest_records(session)` across every `retrieval-log/*/` directory, then `read_bytes()` on each named artefact. **Do NOT use `_logged_payloads`** — it keeps JSON only and would drop the XML that carries abstracts. Refusal names both possibilities: either the payload was never persisted (R10 — retrieve first) or the quote came from memory (section 5(c)). A sibling change added a `status` field to manifest lines; your reader must tolerate its presence and its absence.
- `--to-extraction` must exist, must differ from `--from`, and for `condition_on`/`derived_from` must share `--ref-id` with the asserting row unless `--cross-source` is passed with a reason (a condition drawn from another document is a synthesis act; make it explicit).
- `derive-extraction`: base and delta must share `claimed_unit` unless `--claimed-unit` is given with a `--conversion-note`; and when both parse as numbers, `--claimed-value` must equal base + delta — refuse with both numbers named. A derived figure that disagrees with its own inputs is the defect this verb exists to prevent.

Write the row and its edges in ONE transaction — the `add-term` precedent, where the term and its adjudication land together. Return JSON naming the extraction_id, the figure_role and the edges written.

## Prove it

Work on `cp data/guidebook.db $SCRATCH/w.db` with `GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH` inline. Fault-inject EVERY refusal above and show its message. Then show four happy paths actually writing: a `claim` with `--relation none`; a `finding` with an `insufficient` edge to a `--to-label` (use REF-00784's real quote about Accessibility Guidelines, which is in `retrieval-log/session_2026-09-12-b5b-scope-rulings/f5d94e0feaa8d48f.xml`); a `condition` with a `condition_on` edge to another row; and a `derive-extraction` that correctly refuses because no base row exists. Confirm `sha256sum data/guidebook.db` is unchanged at the end.

Also run `python3 scripts/tests/test_db_integrity.py` and `python3 scripts/run_checks.py --selftest` — both must stay green.

## Report

Every flag and refusal with file:line, the fault-injection output for each, the happy paths, anything you chose not to build and why. If part of this brief is wrong or unsafe, say so and leave it undone — a reasoned refusal beats a forced edit. Do not commit.

You own: `tools/regenerate_vetting_surface.py`, a NEW file `scripts/audit/extraction_relations_integrity.py`, `governance/check-registry.yaml`, and `governance/pipeline-contract.yaml`. Do NOT touch `scripts/db.py` or `scripts/dbcore.py` — another agent owns them. Make the edits, PROVE them, then STOP: do NOT git commit, do NOT git push. The orchestrator verifies and commits.

Read CLAUDE.md first. Binding hardest here: section 5(a) (a gate that passes having examined nothing is failure mode one — every check must print `EXAMINED: <n>`), section 8 (before adding a check, state what wrong thing reaches the GUIDEBOOK if it does not exist; and nothing is added without naming what reads it), rule 7 (no hand-written counts in derived documents), and that adding a check means editing `governance/check-registry.yaml` and never a workflow.

## Context

Migration 075 landed today. Read `scripts/migrations/075_extraction_relations.sql` first — its comments carry the vocabulary meanings. It added `figure_role` (`claim|finding|condition|derived`) and `comparator` to `source_value_extractions`, the junction `extraction_relations`, and the view `v_derived_figure_check` which recomputes a derived figure from its `base` and `delta` inputs where units agree.

Both new columns are nullable and **every one of the 8 live extraction rows has `figure_role` NULL** — they predate the migration and are ungraded. A writer for these columns is being built in parallel by another agent; assume it will exist.

## 1. The reader that makes the data visible

`tools/regenerate_vetting_surface.py` is the human review surface (it currently renders extractions around lines 132-303 and 592-603 — verify for yourself). Add `figure_role` and `comparator` to its queries and display, render the value as `comparator + claimed_value + claimed_unit` where a comparator exists (so "more than thirty centimetres" shows as `> 30 cm`, not `30 cm`), and add a relations column listing each edge as `relation → (row #M | "label") [stated]`. An ungraded row must be visibly ungraded, not blank-and-ambiguous.

This tool is invoked by `scripts/regenerate_derived.sh` and has a `--check` gate; after your change, run the script and confirm both its `--check` gates come back clean.

## 2. The gate

Create `scripts/audit/extraction_relations_integrity.py` and register it in `governance/check-registry.yaml`.

**What wrong thing reaches the guidebook without it** — put this in the script's docstring in your own words, having satisfied yourself it is true: a determination can be computed from rows whose role nobody ever stated, so a tested rig setting or a finding that a code is inadequate can silently govern a cell as though it asserted a value; and a derived figure's stored number can drift from the inputs it claims to be computed from.

It must fail on:
- any `source_value_extractions` row with `figure_role IS NULL` **created after migration 075 was applied**. Determine 075's apply timestamp from `data_migrations` or the schema-migration record rather than hardcoding a date — find how `migrate_db.py` records applications and read it. Rows older than that are REPORTED as `UNGRADED: n`, not failed, until the backfill lands; put a clearly-marked single-line guard in the code so the orchestrator can flip it off in the backfill commit, and say so in the registry entry.
- any `figure_role='derived'` row with no `derived_from` edge carrying `input_role='base'`.
- any row of `v_derived_figure_check` where `recomputed IS NOT NULL AND recomputed <> CAST(stored AS REAL)` — a derived figure disagreeing with its own inputs.
- any `figure_role='condition'` row that is the target of nothing and the source of no `condition_on` edge — an orphan condition, which is a condition on nothing.

It must print `EXAMINED: <n>` naming what it actually looked at, and it must report a zero-subject run as nothing-in-scope rather than as a pass. Read two or three existing scripts in `scripts/audit/` first and follow their output conventions and exit-code discipline exactly.

**Registry entry:** battery `db_integrity`, level `blocking`, `kinds` matching its subject, and a `basis:` that RESOLVES — the registry encodes stage-qualified `basis: <stage>/<criterion>` refs and `run_checks.py --selftest` C7 fails on one that does not resolve. Add the criterion to `governance/pipeline-contract.yaml` under the **judgment** stage (a criterion like `judgment/figure-role-stated`). Declare `min_items` or a `no_floor` with a stated reason — C8 enforces that every check declares one.

**A caution the last agent learned the hard way:** `tools/pipeline-completeness-dashboard.html` renders `pipeline-contract.yaml`'s per-stage enforcement ratio directly, so adding a criterion changes that dashboard and `pipeline_completeness_fresh` (blocking) goes red until you re-run `scripts/regenerate_derived.sh`. Also regenerate `governance/context-map.yaml` with `scripts/generate/context_map.py` rather than hand-editing it.

## Prove it

- Fault-inject each failure condition on a scratch copy (`cp data/guidebook.db $SCRATCH/r.db`, `GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH` inline): insert a post-075 row with NULL `figure_role`; a `derived` row with no base edge; a `v_derived_figure_check` mismatch; an orphan `condition` row. Show the check red for each, and green when removed.
- Show the check reporting the 8 pre-075 rows as UNGRADED without failing.
- `python3 scripts/run_checks.py --selftest` PASS (C7 basis resolution, C8 floor).
- `python3 scripts/run_checks.py --list` shows your check registered at the right level.
- `bash scripts/regenerate_derived.sh` ends `--check`-clean.
- Confirm `sha256sum data/guidebook.db` unchanged.

## Report

What you created and changed with file:line, each proof's output, how you found 075's apply timestamp, and anything you chose not to do and why. If any part of this is wrong or would add apparatus that fails section 8's bar, say so and leave it undone. Do not commit.

Both building.

**Writers** (`db.py`): `--figure-role` and `--comparator` on `add-extraction`, plus three new verbs — `relate-extraction` (with a `--repoint` mode so an "ADAAG" label edge becomes a real row pointer once ADA §405 is admitted), `amend-extraction` (role and comparator only — a wrong value is a second row and a contest, not an overwrite), and `derive-extraction` (refuses when the stored value disagrees with base + delta).

**Readers**: the vetting surface gains the role, the comparator-qualified value (so REF-00976 renders `> 30 cm`, not `30 cm`) and the relations column; plus a new **blocking** check `extraction_relations_integrity` that fails on an ungraded post-075 row, a derived figure with no base input, a derived value that disagrees with its own inputs, and an orphan condition. It's date-guarded so the 8 pre-075 rows report as UNGRADED rather than failing — with a single-line guard I can flip off in the backfill commit.

- **#5 `insufficient`** → *"current Accessibility Guidelines for Buildings and Facilities

stock's own width is not in the abstract, so the base figure does not exist as a row and
`derive-extraction` must refuse. That refusal is correct: a derived figure exists only when its base
does. The J-STAGE full text is the retrieval that would supply it.

`test_db_integrity`'s K01 hashes `n_extractions` **per parameter**. Rows 3b and 7b are new rows on

ships with a compensating restamp migration recomputing both shas by K01's own payload formula, or
waits for the supersede path. K01's own remedy text says "re-run the engine and restamp", and the
engine refuses to re-determine — so restamp is the available route and the state does not change,
only the attestation.

*ramp run* has no term. The ruled path is open: `observe-term` on REF-00980's "30-foot ramp" or
REF-00979's "7.3m long", then `add-term`, then `add-parameter`. *Landing length* has **no phrase in

The writers are in — `c4efa66`. The extraction table can finally take a row.

**The defect I caught in verification, which matters more than the feature:** `derive-extraction` passed the *derived* row's `claim_text` as the quote on both input edges. A derived row's `claim_text` is the analyst's computation statement — words no source ever said — so the byte-substring check could never pass it. **The verb was structurally unable to succeed**, and only its refusal path had been exercised, so nothing revealed it. A verb that can only refuse is worse than a missing one, because it looks implemented.

Each edge now carries its own *target's* quote, which already passed that check when the target row was written. That's an application of the rule rather than a carve-out — and it's the truer record, since the warrant for "this derives from that" is what *that* says. Both SELECTs needed `claim_text` added or the fix would have thrown a KeyError; I checked rather than assumed.

**Two limitations recorded rather than quietly fixed:**

- The quote check **isn't ref-scoped**. The manifest carries no structured `ref_id` — every mention is free text in `purpose` — so a quote genuinely retrieved for one source verifies for a different one. It still blocks the 2026-08-19 shape (text from memory); it doesn't block mis-attribution between two real sources.
- `derive-extraction`'s cross-source refusal **names `--cross-source`, a flag it doesn't accept**. An error message naming a remedy that doesn't exist — rule 4's unswept-caller shape in miniature.

The readers agent is still working: the vetting surface, the new blocking check, and the registry entry are all mid-write.

Confirmed, and it's a serious defect. Watch:

```
A) ungraded row created 02:45, boundary 01:10  →  VERDICT: FAIL, exit 1   ✓ correct
B) an unrelated data migration lands at 03:00  →  VERDICT: CLEAN, exit 0   ✗ same row
```

**The gate un-fires itself.** A defect it correctly caught becomes invisible the moment any later data migration lands — and every batch lands one. Worse, because rows are written to a scratch and *then* carried by a migration applied afterwards, **every row written through the sanctioned path is before the boundary by construction**. It's a blocking gate that cannot catch the case it exists for, giving false assurance. That's §5(a).

The grandfathered set isn't a time range — it's a known, finite list of eight row IDs. Fixing it to be exactly that.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# BACKFILL GUARD (single line, per the orchestrator's own instruction: flip
# this to False in the commit that backfills figure_role on the pre-075 rows,
# and nowhere else). While True: a figure_role-NULL row created at-or-before
# the migration-075 boundary computed below is reported as UNGRADED and does
# NOT fail this check. Once False: every figure_role-NULL row fails, full
# stop, and the boundary is never consulted.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
PRE_075_GRANDFATHER = True


def _parse_ts(raw):
    """Parse either timestamp form this database actually uses into an aware
    UTC datetime, or None if it parses as neither.

      - data_migrations.applied_at: ISO-8601 with a UTC offset, e.g.
        '2026-09-13T01:10:06+00:00' (migrate_db.py: datetime.now(timezone.utc)
        .isoformat(timespec='seconds')).
      - source_value_extractions.created_at: naive, minute precision, always
        UTC, e.g. '2026-09-13 01:07' (scripts/dbcore.py: now() ->
        strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M")).

    datetime.fromisoformat handles both directly (Python's isoformat parser
    accepts the space-separated form as well as 'T'); a naive result is
    stamped UTC rather than left ambiguous, because every writer of either
    column in this codebase is UTC-only.
    """
    if raw is None:
        return None
    raw = raw.strip()
    if not raw:
        return None
    try:
        dt = datetime.fromisoformat(raw)
    except ValueError:
        return None
    if dt.tzinfo is None:
        dt = dt.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
    return dt.astimezone(timezone.utc)


def migration_075_boundary(con):
    """MAX(data_migrations.applied_at) — see the module docstring for why this,
    and not a git log, and not a literal date, is the boundary. None if the
    ledger is empty or unparseable, which the caller treats as "cannot run".
    """
    rows = con.execute(
        f"SELECT applied_at FROM {LEDGER} WHERE applied_at IS NOT NULL"
    ).fetchall()
    parsed = [t for t in (_parse_ts(r[0]) for r in rows) if t is not None]
    return max(parsed) if parsed else None


def main() -> int:
    if not os.path.exists(DB):
        print(f"FAIL: no database at {DB}")
        return 2

printf 'judgment: six figures graded and three baselines recorded — and the two that could not land, with the reason [%s]\n\n' "$(date -u '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M')" > /tmp/m6.txt
cat >> /tmp/m6.txt <<'MSG'
The first rows the project has ever carried that say what KIND of thing a figure
is, and what it is stated against.

Six of eight extractions graded `finding`, and three baseline edges recorded, each
quoting the sentence that establishes it:

  REF-00784  insufficient -> "current Accessibility Guidelines for Buildings and
             Facilities specifications"  [standard/named]
  REF-00971  insufficient -> "existing standards"  [unnamed/UNNAMED]
  REF-00981  audited_against -> "The Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990"

REF-00971's is the one worth noticing: the source measures against a ruler it
never names, and that is now a queryable fact rather than an absence nobody could
see. "Unstated baseline" and "no baseline" are different things and the schema can
finally tell them apart.

TWO ROWS DID NOT LAND, AND THE REASON IS THE FINDING OF THIS COMMIT.

Extractions 1 and 3 are conditions -- rig settings, not claims. Extraction 1 is the
four slopes a treadmill was SET to; extraction 3 is the ADA range REF-00980
TESTED, which its own abstract says in as many words. Grading them truthfully made
extraction_relations_integrity refuse the backfill: a condition must condition
something, and neither target existed, because neither study's actual FINDING had
ever been extracted. The gate was right and the corpus was thin.

That question just paid for itself. Here's what merging would publish:

```
spec 1 (ramp gradient) — STATED at T1, the project's strongest claim
   REF-00973  extraction 1  → a CONDITION (the slopes a treadmill was set to)
   REF-00974  extraction 2  → finding, claim_type ABSENT — asserts nothing at all
   REF-00979  extraction 4  → finding
   REF-00980  extraction 3  → a CONDITION (the ADA range the study TESTED)

spec 2 (corridor width) — provisional
   all four governing rows → finding
```

**Not one governing row of either determination is a `claim`.** Specification 1 is `stated` at full T1 strength, governed entirely by two rig settings and two findings — one of which asserts nothing. And under your ruling today, an `insufficient` finding supplies **direction, not value** — so specification 2 has no value-supplying row either.

Both are surfaced by `v_best_practice`.

So the answer to your question is: **the research isn't what's wrong — the determinations are.** And they're not wrong records; they're accurate records of what an engine computed under a rule set that your rulings tonight superseded. Un-committing them would be rewriting the log, which this project forbids for good reason — and they're also the things that surfaced every defect tonight.

The real exposure is narrower and fixable: **the render path will publish a determination that has no value-supplying row.** Three ways to handle it:

1. **Merge as-is.** Main publishes both. I don't recommend it — the book would carry a ● T1 claim resting on rig settings.
2. **Hold the whole PR.** Loses the migration, the writers, the gate, four closed defects and the tier corrections, all of which are verified and independently good.
3. **Merge everything, and put one guard on the render boundary:** `v_best_practice` does not surface a determination unless at least one governing row is `figure_role IN ('claim','derived')`. Both determinations then drop out of the book automatically and reappear when the engine is fixed and re-determines them — no data deleted, no record rewritten, and the guard is the engine rule from the design applied one layer out.

I'd take 3. It's small, it's principled, and without it the §8 harm is concrete: the guidebook prints "therefore 1:12 ●" on evidence that never said so.

Your call — it changes what the book shows, which is yours rather than mine.

content.text:
Decisive, and it changes the ordering of your plan:

```
gather_sources:  WHERE x.parameter_id = ?     ← and nothing else
figure_role / comparator in the engine:  no matches
```

**The engine reads none of the grading.** So deleting the determinations and re-running *as things stand* would gather exactly the same rows — conditions included — and rebuild the same wrong answer. The machinery that got updated tonight is the schema and the writers; the engine is untouched at the point where it decides.

Your plan is right. The order has to be **engine first, then delete, then re-run** — otherwise it's a no-op on the actual defect.

And the minimal correct engine change is smaller than it sounds. Today `gather_sources` returns every source holding any extraction for the parameter. It should return only rows that **supply a value** — `figure_role IN ('claim','derived')`. Apply that to the current corpus and both cells have **zero** value-supplying rows, so both fall to `pending`. Which is the truth: not one retrieved source states a corridor width or a ramp gradient value. The cells have been `stated` and `provisional` on evidence that never said so.

That one predicate makes the pipeline honest immediately. The richer behaviour your rulings define — findings supplying direction, `confirms` upgrading a code value, the floored-mean band for derived figures — builds on top of it rather than being required for it.

So I'd sequence it: **(1)** the `gather_sources` predicate plus the `pending` path; **(2)** a compensating migration deleting both determinations, their convergence rows and source links — which also frees `idx_spec_row_identity` and removes K01's subject, unblocking rows 1 and 3; **(3)** grade 1 and 3 and extract the findings they condition; **(4)** re-run both cells and show the determinations that come out.

Want me to run that sequence now? Step 1 is where your five rulings start to bite, so I'd rather you see the predicate before I delete anything.

def gather_sources(conn, parameter_id):
    """The sources holding an EXTRACTION FOR THIS PARAMETER. Not the slug's sources.

    THE DEFECT THIS CLOSES, measured 2026-09-10. This function took a `slug` and
    joined `source_slug_links`, so the governing set was "everything admitted to this
    topic". `parameter_id` was carried through determine()'s signature, sha(), the
    report dict and validate_parameter() and never reached the evidence at all -- the
    071 re-key was cosmetic at the exact point where the engine decides. The visible
    result was `param 1 x MOB -> stated basis=T1+CO1+T2` anchored on all 10 sources
    linked to `accessible-circulation-geometry`, 8 of which the engine's own report
    flagged `tier_inconsistent`, and every one of the 10 DOWN-WEIGHTED.

    The cause was one absent table-writer, not a bad query: `db.py` held ZERO
    references to `source_value_extractions`, so no parameter->evidence edge existed
    and the slug was the only join available. `db.py add-extraction` (migration 073,
    same change as this) creates the edge; this query uses it.

    DISTINCT IS LOAD-BEARING, not tidiness. Evidence to judgment is 1:N (D-0168): one
    code document yields many clause-level extractions for one parameter. Without
    DISTINCT, NBC 3.8's clauses would each add a copy of the same source to the
    governing set, and a single document would look like corroboration of itself --
    the independence failure `v_value_independence` exists to detect, manufactured
    inside the engine.

    A CONSEQUENCE WORTH STATING, because it is stop condition 6 of the operative
    plan ("any `stated` cell whose governing set includes a source with no extraction
    for that parameter -- do not merge the migration"): after this change that cell is
    not merely forbidden, it is unconstructible. Every ref_id in the governing set
    came out of this query, and this query returns only sources that hold an
    extraction for the parameter being determined.
    """
    # verification_disposition arrived with migration 049 (D-0157). This script
    # is run against scratch and fixture databases as well as the canonical one
    # -- it refuses the canonical DB by design -- so the column is selected only
    # when it exists. A pre-049 database still disqualifies correctly through
    # the legacy status values in DISQUALIFIED.
    has_disp = any(r[1] == "verification_disposition"
                   for r in conn.execute("PRAGMA table_info(evidence_sources)"))
    disp_col = "e.verification_disposition" if has_disp else "NULL"
    q = f"""SELECT DISTINCT e.ref_id, e.tier, e.evidence_type, e.co1_source_type,
                   e.verification_status, {disp_col}, e.scope, e.jurisdiction
            FROM source_value_extractions x
            JOIN evidence_sources e ON e.ref_id = x.ref_id
            WHERE x.parameter_id = ? AND e.superseded_by_ref_id IS NULL
            ORDER BY e.ref_id"""
    return [dict(zip(("ref_id", "tier", "evidence_type", "co1_source_type",
                      "verification_status", "verification_disposition",
                      "scope", "jurisdiction"), r))
            for r in conn.execute(q, (parameter_id,))]

    ONLY VALUE-SUPPLYING ROWS GOVERN (added 2026-09-13, migration 075's whole point).

    corpus the day the grading landed: specification 1 was `stated` at T1 -- the
    strongest claim this project makes -- on four rows of which TWO WERE CONDITIONS
    (the slopes a treadmill was set to; the ADA range a study tested) and two were
    findings, one of them `claim_type='absent'`, asserting nothing whatever. Not one
    governing row was a claim. Specification 2 was the same shape.

    So the predicate is `figure_role IN ('claim','derived')`:

      claim     -- the row states a value for the parameter. Governs.
      derived   -- the row's value was computed from other rows. Governs; its band
                   is the floored mean of its inputs' (owner ruling 2026-09-13).
      finding   -- the row reports something ABOUT the parameter without asserting a
                   value: "code-compliant width fails 10-100% of users". Supplies
                   DIRECTION, never value (owner ruling 2026-09-13). Not gathered here.
      condition -- a rig setting or a limit the value is conditioned by. Never anchors.
      NULL      -- ungraded. Not a value-supplier: a row nobody has stated the kind of
                   cannot be read as a claim, which is exactly how a tested slope came
                   to govern a `stated` cell.

    A cell whose value-supplying set is empty now comes out `pending`, which for both
    live cells is the truth -- not one retrieved source states a corridor width or a
    ramp gradient value. Gathering `finding` rows for direction, and the `confirms`
    edge that upgrades a code value, build ON this predicate and are not required by
    it.
    """'''

-- Compensating deletion of the project's two determinations, 2026-09-13.
--
-- WHY THIS IS NOT REWRITING THE RECORD. A specification is DERIVED OUTPUT: the

-- and assess_cell.py computes it from the extractions. Deleting derived output and
-- re-deriving it is regeneration, not deletion of evidence. Nothing that was
-- OBSERVED is touched: every source, search, candidate, observation, population
-- match and extraction stays exactly as it is. The migrations that created these
-- rows stay in history; this one removes them; a rebuild replays both and lands in
-- the correct state, which is the sanctioned fix-forward pattern.
--
-- WHY THEY MUST GO. Migration 075 gave a figure a role, and grading the live rows
-- showed what these determinations actually rested on. Specification 1 was `stated`
-- at T1 -- the strongest claim this project makes -- on four rows of which two were

-- convergence rows the specifications pointed at.

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /tmp/claude-0/bundled-skills/2.1.270/6f1c58e2e2a1d2d74123d1a4bdd9ab70/verify

**Verification is runtime observation.** You build the app, run it,
drive it to where the changed code executes, and capture what you
see. That capture is your evidence. Nothing else is.

**Don't run tests. Don't typecheck.** Running them here proves you
can run CI — not that the change works. Not as a warm-up,
not "just to be sure," not as a regression sweep after. The time
goes to running the app instead.

**Don't import-and-call.** `import { foo } from './src/...'` then
`console.log(foo(x))` is a unit test you wrote. The function did what
the function does — you knew that from reading it. The app never ran.
Whatever calls `foo` in the real codebase ends at a CLI, a socket, or
a window. Go there.

## Find the change

The scope is what you're verifying — usually a diff, sometimes just
"does X work." In a git repo, establish the full range (a branch may
be many commits, or the change may still be uncommitted):

```bash
git log --oneline @{u}..              # count commits (if upstream set)
git diff @{u}.. --stat                # full range, not HEAD~1
git diff origin/HEAD... --stat        # no upstream: committed vs base
git diff HEAD --stat                  # uncommitted: working tree vs HEAD
gh pr diff                            # if in a PR context
```

State the commit count. Large diff truncating? Redirect to a file
then Read it. Repo but no diff from any of these → say so, stop.
**No repo → the scope is whatever the user named; ask if they
didn't.**

**The diff is ground truth. Any description is a claim about it.**
Read both. If they disagree, that's a finding.

## Surface

The surface is where a user — human or programmatic — meets the
change. That's where you observe.

| Change reaches | Surface | You |
|---|---|---|
| CLI / TUI | terminal | type the command, capture the pane — [example](examples/cli.md) |
| Server / API | socket | send the request, capture the response — [example](examples/server.md) |
| GUI | pixels | drive it under xvfb/Playwright, screenshot |
| Library | package boundary | sample code through the public export — `import pkg`, not `import ./src/...` |
| Prompt / agent config | the agent | run the agent, capture its behavior |
| CI workflow | Actions | dispatch it, read the run |

**Internal function? Not a surface.** Something in the repo calls it
and that caller ends at one of the rows above. Follow it there. A
bash security gate's surface isn't the function's return value — it's
the CLI prompting or auto-allowing when you type the command.

**No runtime surface at all** — docs-only, type declarations with no
emit, build config that produces no behavioral diff — report
**SKIP — no runtime surface: (reason).** Don't run tests to fill
the space.

**Tests in the diff are the author's evidence, not a surface.** CI
runs them. You'd be re-running CI. Tests-only PR → SKIP, one line.
Mixed src+tests → verify the src, ignore the test files. Reading a
test to learn what to check is fine — it's a spec. But then go run
the app. Checking that assertions match source is code review.

## Get a handle

**Check `.claude/skills/` first — even if you already know how to
build and run.** A matching `verifier-*` skill is the repo's
evidence-capture protocol: it wraps the session so a reviewer can
replay what you saw (recording, screenshots). Drive the surface
without it and you get a verdict with no replay.

Skills live at the repo root **and** in the package/app dirs the
diff touches — in a monorepo the unlock for `apps/desktop/` is
usually `apps/desktop/.claude/skills/`, not the root. Probe both:

```bash
ls .claude/skills/                    # repo root
ls <touched-dir>/.claude/skills/      # each dir level the diff names
```

- **`verifier-*` matching your surface** (CLI verifier for a CLI
  change, etc.) → invoke it with the Skill tool and follow its
  setup. Mismatched surface → skip that one, try the next. Stale
  verifier (fails on mechanics unrelated to the change) → ask the
  user whether to patch it; don't FAIL the change for verifier rot.
- **`run-*` but no matching verifier** → use its build/launch
  primitives as your handle.
- **Neither** → cold start from README/package.json/Makefile. Timebox
  ~15min. Stuck → BLOCKED with exactly where, plus a filled-in
  `/run-skill-generator` prompt. Got through → **persist what you
  learned**: create `.claude/skills/verify/SKILL.md` at the level you
  probed above — repo root for a single-package repo; the touched
  package/app dir (`apps/desktop/.claude/skills/verify/SKILL.md`) in
  a monorepo where verification is per-package — capturing the
  build/launch/drive recipe that worked, so the next session skips
  this cold start. Keep it short: the commands that worked, the
  flows worth driving, any gotchas. A project verify skill already
  exists → edit it only when it steered you wrong: a documented
  command failed or turned out wrong, or a needed step it doesn't
  cover. Routine learnings don't warrant an edit, and never rewrite
  or reorganize existing content for style.

## Drive it

Smallest path that makes the changed code execute:

- Changed a flag? Run with it.
- Changed a handler? Hit that route.
- Changed error handling? Trigger the error.
- Changed an internal function? Find the CLI command / request / render
  that reaches it. Run that.

**Read your plan back before running.** If every step is build /
typecheck / run test file — you've planned a CI rerun, not a
verification. Find a step that reaches the surface or report BLOCKED.

**The verdict is table stakes. Your observations are the signal.**
A PASS with three sharp "hey, I noticed…" lines is worth more than a
bare PASS. You're the only reviewer who actually *ran* the thing —
anything that made you pause, work around, or go "huh" is information
the author doesn't have. Don't filter for "is this a bug." Filter for
"would I mention this if they were sitting next to me."

**End-to-end, through the real interface.** Pieces passing in
isolation doesn't mean the flow works — seams are where bugs hide.
If users click buttons, test by clicking buttons, not by curling the
API underneath.

**Destructive path?** If the change touches code that deletes,
publishes, sends, or writes outside the workspace and there's no
dry-run or safe target, don't drive it live. Verify what you can
around it and say which path you didn't exercise and why.

## Push on it

The claim checked out — that's the first half. Confirming is step
one, not the job. The description is what the author intended;
your value is what they didn't.

You know exactly what changed. Probe *around* it, at the same
surface you just drove:

- **New flag / option** → empty value, passed twice, combined with a
  conflicting flag, typo'd (does the error name it?)
- **New handler / route** → wrong method, malformed body, missing
  required field, oversized payload
- **Changed error path** → the adjacent errors it didn't touch —
  did the refactor catch them too, or only the one in the diff?
- **Interactive / TUI** → Ctrl-C mid-op, resize the pane, paste
  garbage, rapid-fire the key, Esc at the wrong moment
- **State / persistence** → do it twice, do it with stale state
  underneath, do it in two sessions at once
- **Wander** → what's adjacent? What looked off while you were
  confirming? Go back to it.

These aren't a checklist — pick the ones the change points at. Stop
when you've covered the obvious adjacents or hit something worth a
⚠️. A probe that finds nothing is still a step: "🔍 passed `--from ''`
→ clean `error: --from requires a value`, exit 2." That the author
didn't test it is exactly why it's worth knowing it holds.

Still not a test run. You're at the surface, typing what a user
would type wrong.

## Capture

Stdout, response bodies, screenshots, pane dumps. Captured output is
evidence; your memory isn't. Something unexpected? Don't route around
it — capture, note, decide if it's the change or the environment.
Unrelated breakage is a finding, not noise.

Shared process state (tmux, ports, lockfiles) — isolate. `tmux -L
name`, bind `:0`, `mktemp -d`. You share a namespace with your host.

## Report

Inline, final message:

```
## Verification: <one-line what changed>

**Verdict:** PASS | FAIL | BLOCKED | SKIP

**Claim:** <what it's supposed to do — your read of the diff and/or
the stated claim; note any mismatch>

**Method:** <how you got a handle — which verifier/run-skill, or
cold start; what you launched>

### Steps

Each step is one thing you did to the **running app** and what it
showed. Build/install/checkout are setup, not steps. Test runs and
typecheck don't belong here — they're CI's output.

1. ✅/❌/⚠️/🔍 <what you did to the running app> → <what you observed>
   <evidence: the app's own output — pane capture, response body,
   screenshot>

🔍 marks a probe — a step off the claim's happy path, trying to
break it. At least one. A Steps list that's all ✅ and no 🔍 is a
happy-path replay: still PASS, but you stopped at the first half.

**Screenshot / sample:** <the one frame a reviewer looks at to see
the feature — an image for GUI/TUI, code block for library/API;
omit for build/types-only>

### Findings
<Things you noticed. Not just bugs — friction, surprises, anything
a first-time user would trip on. "Took three tries to find the right
flag." "Error message on typo was unhelpful." "Default seems odd for
the common case." "Works, but slower than I expected." Lower the bar:
if it made you pause, it goes here. But the pause has to be yours,
from running the app — not from reading the PR page. A red CI check,
a review comment, someone else's bot: visible to anyone already, and
you relaying it isn't an observation. Claim/diff mismatch, pre-existing
breakage, and env notes also belong.

Each probe gets a line here even when it held — "🔍 empty `--from`
→ clean error" tells the author what *was* covered, which they
can't see from a bare PASS.

Lead with ⚠️ for lines worth interrupting the reviewer for; plain
bullets are context. Empty is fine if nothing stuck out — but nothing
sticking out is itself rare.>
```

**Evidence has to reach the reader.** A file path is only evidence
if the person reading the report can open it. If the `SendUserFile`
tool is in your toolset, you're on a remote surface where they
can't — send the screenshots and recordings with it and let the
report name what you sent. Without it, reference the path and keep
the evidence that matters inline — pane captures and response
bodies travel in the report; a bare path only works when the reader
shares your filesystem.

**Verdicts:**
- **PASS** — you ran the app, the change did what it should at its
  surface. Not: tests pass, builds clean, code looks right.
- **FAIL** — you ran it and it doesn't. Or it breaks something else.
  Or claim and diff disagree materially.
- **BLOCKED** — couldn't reach a state where the change is observable.
  Build broke, env missing a dep, handle wouldn't come up. Not a
  verdict on the change. Never report an approach blocked or
  impossible until you've enumerated the skills along the touched
  subtree — environment-specific unlocks (headless runners, login
  helpers, VM harnesses) usually live there. Say exactly where it
  stopped + `/run-skill-generator` prompt.
- **SKIP** — no runtime surface exists. Docs-only, types-only,
  tests-only. Nothing went wrong; there's just nothing here to run.
  One line why.

No partial pass. "3 of 4 passed" is FAIL until 4 passes or is
explained away.

**When in doubt, FAIL.** False PASS ships broken code; false FAIL
costs one more human look. Ambiguous output is FAIL with the raw
capture attached — don't interpret.
